title: On Clapping at the end of every song
subtitle: 戏剧表演 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）
meta: 主题语境：戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）　|　核心词汇：clap　|　正文 362 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 clap 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1970 the postman ① clapped at the end of every song without a word of thanks, and every sender in the office said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the postman ② claps at the end of every song at once without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ clap at the end of every song at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ clapped at the end of every song before — a line in the list for June 1964 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Clapping at the end of every song without a word of thanks, the postman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the envelope at the far box, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ clap the boy on the shoulder at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Clap the boy on the shoulder at once and never mention it again.

By 1977 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the list, and a new sender from the next office ⑧ claps the boy on the shoulder without a word of thanks every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the box, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ clapped at the end of every song again when nobody else would.

⑩ To clap at the end of every song, my mother said in 1982, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the office remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the office forgets, somebody claps at the end of every song at once again and somebody must clap at the end of every song without a word of thanks all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 鼓掌（一般过去式 clapped at the end of every song：1970 年邮差头一回这样做，不图一句谢）
B. v. 鼓掌（一般现在 claps at the end of every song：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 鼓掌（不定式 to clap at the end of every song：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 鼓掌（过去完成时 had clapped at the end of every song：1964 年六月的收发清单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 鼓掌（动名词 clapping at the end of every song 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 轻拍（clap the boy on the shoulder：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去轻拍在那孩子肩上轻拍一下）
G. v. 轻拍（clap the boy on the shoulder：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 鼓掌（后段两处：新来的寄信人照例 claps the boy on the shoulder，而母亲又一次 clapped at the end of every song）

answers.why: clap 意为“鼓掌”，1970 年邮差不图一句谢鼓掌每支歌唱罢都拍手，那是邮局里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 clapped。
clap 意为“鼓掌”，自那以后邮差二话不说地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 claps。
clap 意为“鼓掌”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯鼓掌每支歌唱罢都拍手”，此处为不定式 to clap at the end of every song。
clap 意为“鼓掌”，收发清单里 六月 那行字说明早在 1977 年之前就有人鼓掌过，故用过去完成时 had clapped。
clap 意为“鼓掌”，邮差说“鼓掌每支歌唱罢都拍手这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 clapping at the end of every song 作主语。
clap 意为“轻拍”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去轻拍在那孩子肩上轻拍一下”，should ever 之后用原形 clap the boy on the shoulder。
clap 意为“轻拍”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻轻拍在那孩子肩上轻拍一下（clap the boy on the shoulder at once），以后再也不要提起。
clap 意为“鼓掌”，新来的寄信人每个星期都照例轻拍在那孩子肩上轻拍一下，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 claps。
clap 意为“鼓掌”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次不图一句谢鼓掌每支歌唱罢都拍手，用一般过去式 clapped 叙述。
clap 意为“鼓掌”，结尾那句是母亲 1982 年的话：要鼓掌每支歌唱罢都拍手，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和邮局记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 clap 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1970 the postman clapped at the end of every song without a word of thanks, and nobody in the office forgot it.
Even now the postman claps at the end of every song at once whenever the office asks.
Clapping at the end of every song without a word of thanks, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever clap the boy on the shoulder at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new sender from the next office claps the boy on the shoulder without a word of thanks every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother clapped at the end of every song again, and the office remembered that half.
